page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-16 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs, which map to 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

The AMD EPYC processor includes 32 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache. It supports hardware-accelerated instructions such as AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, though it lacks AVX-512 capabilities. In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance via stress-ng, scoring 2674.77. Multi-core performance and memory bandwidth benchmarks, including uncached read and write speeds, fall within the average range.

The instance achieves average scores across a variety of workloads, including software compilation, database operations, and static web serving. It exhibits strong performance in text generation for small language models, reaching 277.2 tokens per second, but drops to average speeds for medium-sized models. Given the balanced resource distribution and lack of local NVMe storage, this server is configured for general-purpose workloads, web serving, and moderate database operations.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-16 is a general-purpose server configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM, utilizing the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. The hardware architecture features 8 physical cores with multithreading, 32 MB of L3 cache, and support for AVX, AES, and SHA_NI instruction sets, though it lacks AVX-512. It contains no local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance and strong text generation speeds for small language models, while multi-core processing, memory bandwidth, and database operations perform in the average tier. This balanced resource profile makes the instance suitable for general-purpose computing, software compilation, static web serving, and moderate database workloads.
